belief: People will think I'm crazy if they know.
origins: Stigma about anxiety, depression, trauma, and other struggles teaches us to hide them. Early experiences of being dismissed, mocked, or whispered about confirm the fear. We pay for the secrecy with isolation.
teaches: Scripture shows faithful people in great distress: “I am weary from groaning; all night I flood my bed with weeping.” “When anxiety overwhelms me, Your consolation delights my soul.” “The LORD is near to the brokenhearted; He saves the contrite in spirit.” Paul writes, “Carry one another’s burdens.” “Two are better than one… if one falls down, his companion can lift him up; but pity the one who falls without another to help him up!” Sharing wisely with safe people brings relief. Not everyone will understand, but God does, and many will.
self_statements: They will see me as unstable.
I have to keep it a secret.
I am the only one this happens to.
errors: Believing others see me as either normal or crazy.
Assuming I know how people will react.
Feeling ashamed and concluding that I am defective.
questions: Who has responded well when I have shared something hard?
What exactly do I fear they will think?
Who are the safest people to tell?
How common are these struggles, even among believers?
What does Scripture show about distress and God’s nearness?
What small piece could I share first?
truth: Struggling does not make me crazy. Many faithful people have suffered distress, and God is near. I can choose safe people, share at my own pace, and find relief and help.
hw_truths: God is near to the brokenhearted.
Faithful people have wept and groaned.
I can share at my own pace.
log: Each week, note one thing you shared and how it went.
actions: Write two or three trustworthy people.
Talk with a counselor. If you ever think of harming yourself, call or text 988 (U.S.) right away.
prayer: Lord, I fear being judged. You are near to the brokenhearted. Give me safe people and the courage to share a little at a time. Amen.
name_example: Sarah can write: “When anxiety overwhelms me, God’s consolation delights my soul.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “People will think I'm crazy if they know.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
